newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude moribund with no deals heard.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude moribund with no deals heard.

text.p: The Brent market was very quiet on Friday with no new deals reported on either the North Sea physical market or the forward paper market but numbers were notionally steady, traders said.

January Brent cargoes were assessed around screen levels of $22.50/55 a barrel in the London morning, slightly weaker from Thursday's close. Forward intermonth spreads were firmer, with Jan/Feb talked at +59/+61 cents, two cents higher than the previous day.
CFD levels also firmed after all three Brent dates which turned wet on Thursday were kept by the equity holders.
Next week's dates were discussed at Jan Brent +25/+30 cents, up from +22/+25 cents on Thursday.
NYMEX has been closed since Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday, depriving the London futures market of direction and deterring any aggressive business.
Wet Brent was untraded but was seen valued at January Brent +35 cents in line with the last reported deal this week, a trader said. Three Brent dates were doing the paper rounds on Friday.
"Nothing has traded but North Sea differentials are still firm," the trader added.

A flurry of buying activity late last week mopped up much of the early December loading cargoes while the tightness of Urals supplies in the Med was also seen as supportive of the wet market as refiners shopped around for West African and North Sea grades.
"There has been nothing traded in the Med yesterday or today but then there is not much on offer," a Med trader said, referring to delays at Russia's main oil port of Novorossiisk on the Black Sea.
